title: Draft-and-Audit Reinforcement Learning for Optimization Modeling
claim: Learning a two-turn draft-then-audit workflow, rewarded only by one final execution, teaches the model to revise its own outputs.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right flow, feedback loop on top returning to policy updates
description: A single wide flow diagram reads left to right. A problem description box (a factory making tables and chairs) at top left feeds a blue Policy box labeled Turn 1: Draft. That produces a Draft Program box with code that has integer-type errors and commented-out missing constraints. A dashed green Audit Rubric box (check constraints, verify parameters, review domains) and a large blue arrow lead to Turn 2: Audit, where an orange Policy box produces an Audited Program. Its code is fixed, with integer variables and constraints added. Another large arrow leads to a Single Terminal Execution box that runs the program, gets a result, and assigns a binary reward (1 or red 0). An RL Algorithm box at top right sends Update arrows back to both policy boxes. The eye goes first to the code boxes and the large arrows.
caption: DA-RL overview (Draft→Audit with terminal-only verification). Given a word problem x, the policy first generates a draft
abstract: Natural language to optimization (NL2Opt) requires translating unstructured text into executable mathematical models. Beyond simple syntax errors, this task suffers from silent modeling failures, where incorrect formulations execute successfully but yield invalid results. We propose \textbf{Draft-and-Audit RL (DA-RL)}, a framework that learns optimization modeling as a two-step iterative workflow. Unlike inference-time scaffolds that rely on intermediate solver feedback to guide repairs, DA-RL optimizes a shared-parameter policy using terminal-only verification: the model is rewarded solely based on the execution of the final audited program. This constraint forces the model to internalize rubric-guided revision as a learned capability and encourages the emergence of cross-turn synergy, where the policy learns to generate drafts that are structurally amenable to self-correction.
